summary: 100-foot Wisconsin standard tower built June 1932 in Shawano County; listed as standing, with no staffing or access record found.

facts.design: Wisconsin standard tower with an external protected ladder

events.note: Built June 1932 per the NHLR detail page

evidence.supports: 100-foot Wisconsin standard tower with external protected ladder, built June 1932
evidence.quote: This 100-foot Wisconsin standard tower features an external protected ladder. It was built in June 1932.

evidence.supports: administered by the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources
many Wisconsin towers still standing were built in the 1930s by CCC crews (general context; not confirmed for this tower)
evidence.quote: Many of the towers we see still standing today were built during the 1930s by the young men of the Civilian Conservation Corps.

evidence.supports: towers manned May to September for many decades; staffing later reduced to the peak fire season
evidence.quote: Manned from May to September for many decades, their staffing was reduced to the peak forest fire season, between snow melt and green up in the spring.

evidence.supports: 72 towers still in use were decommissioned in 2015 (general; not confirmed for this tower)
evidence.quote: In 2015, the 72 aging towers still in use were decommissioned.

evidence.supports: some towers dismantled, many remain as monuments
evidence.quote: Some have been dismantled, but many remain as a monument to their service.

evidence.supports: listed as standing by the Forest Fire Lookout Association
evidence.quote: Kolpack Shawano 44.92134 -89.00690 Tower Standing NHLR US 1219, WI 25

sources.title: Connecting the dots: the fire towers of Wisconsin

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Kolpack-specific facts come only from the NHLR detail page (build month, height, registration, administrator) and the FFLA state list (standing). Two searches found no newspaper, DNR or staffing source for this tower. Access, staffing and any rental are not established, and the story says so. Worth a search of the Shawano County Historical Society archive (its digital archive appeared in results) before a fuller history. The record's 'access: unknown' stands.
